scene: Street-level side view of a blue public bus stopped on a paved road, with several passengers (at least 2) standing at the door boarding/exiting.
rubric: Report should (1) identify the scene as a public bus at a stop, (2) acknowledge passengers boarding/alighting, (3) flag potential pedestrian safety concerns (people near road), (4) follow the 4-section structure exactly (Scene, Object Inventory, Detector Gaps, Risk Assessment).

scene: Aerial top-down view of a building under active construction: concrete foundation, exposed rebar, wooden forms, construction equipment (excavator, crane), surrounding dirt and a paved road.
rubric: Report should (1) identify the overhead/aerial view, (2) describe an active construction site, (3) explicitly mention safety hazards typical of construction: open foundation, exposed rebar, heavy equipment, fall risk, (4) note that the aerial perspective causes a domain gap for the COCO-trained detector (small objects, top-down view not in training data), (5) classify risk as high.

scene: Aerial top-down view of a very large rectangular building with white/grey roof panels, surrounded by ongoing construction work (debris, scaffolding, dirt).
rubric: Report should (1) recognize the large building footprint from aerial view, (2) note ongoing construction activity around it, (3) acknowledge domain gap (top-down roof view unlikely to match COCO classes), (4) flag any debris or unfinished sections as safety concerns, (5) classify risk as medium-to-high.

scene: Aerial view of a marina with dozens of boats (yachts and small craft) docked in slips along piers, surrounded by dark blue water and a stone breakwater.
rubric: Report should (1) identify the marina / boat dock scene, (2) note the many boats, (3) explain the domain gap: boats at this top-down angle and scale are likely missed by COCO detector, (4) classify risk as low (no immediate hazards in this well-organized static view), (5) do not fabricate hazard detections.

scene: Aerial view of an industrial site on red/orange soil with several trucks (dump trucks, tankers), construction materials, and tire tracks.
rubric: Report should (1) identify the industrial / construction site, (2) note the trucks and heavy equipment, (3) flag safety concerns: unpaved soft ground (tip-over risk), equipment operating near workers, dust, (4) classify risk as high.

scene: Front view of a group of children (about 5-6) standing in front of a large tree outdoors in daylight.
rubric: Report should (1) identify children / young people in an outdoor setting, (2) acknowledge the detector likely reported them as 'person' class, (3) flag supervision/safety considerations for children, (4) classify risk as medium (no immediate hazard but vulnerable subjects).

scene: Aerial top-down view of a parking lot with rows of parked cars, painted lane markings, and a few trees.
rubric: Report should (1) identify the parking lot scene, (2) note the many cars detected, (3) explain that the top-down view is a domain gap but cars in side-view would be detected well, (4) classify risk as low (static, organized, no hazards visible).

scene: Aerial view of a port/harbor with construction cranes, partially built structures, and water in the background.
rubric: Report should (1) identify port/harbor with construction activity, (2) note the cranes and partially built infrastructure, (3) flag safety concerns (heavy lifting, working near water, incomplete structures), (4) classify risk as high.

scene: Aerial view of an industrial site with construction equipment, debris, dirt, and scattered materials.
rubric: Report should (1) identify the industrial/construction site, (2) note scattered materials and equipment, (3) flag safety concerns (unorganized site, trip hazards, heavy equipment), (4) classify risk as high.

scene: Beach/coastal view with 3 people walking on wet sand near the water's edge in daylight.
rubric: Report should (1) identify the beach/coastal scene with people, (2) note 3 persons walking, (3) optionally mention tidal/slip risks (low), (4) classify risk as low.
